title: Add `test_ray` function: a version of intersect_ray that has optional result parameter
body:
Note (22/07/2025):
- After searching around other PRs I've found that this is probably redundant once struct are easier to add (https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/108503). The performance gain is going to be similar to the struct version, but the struct version doesn't require pre-allocating a result object. So depending on the time frame this PR might not be useful.


Problem:
- When profiling my game I found that most time in intersect_ray is spend on creating and filling in the Dictionary that is returned.
- Often in my game code I only need to know if the ray hit anything and don't care about the data in the Dictionary.
- My game uses raycasts for everything from bullets, AI to level generation, any speedup would be great.

Solution:
- User has to pass a OPTIONAL result object to the function
- This change mimics how physicsserver3d body_test_motion is implemented.
- bonus: result object can be preallocated and reused similar to PhysicsRayQueryParameters3D (no C# garbage)

First tests give a big performance speedup in both GDscript and C# when ray hits a surface. (~5x faster in release export)
It is even slightly faster when no result object is passed.

(These tests reuse the result object instead of allocating a new one each time. This is also how I use PhysicsRayQueryParameters3D in a game project.)


Example usage:

As replacement for intersect_ray with better performance:
```gdscript
var params = PhysicsRayQueryParameters3D.create(Vector3.ZERO, Vector3(0, 0, 100))
var ray_result = PhysicsTestRayResult3D.new()
if (space_state.test_ray(params, ray_result)):
    print("position: ", ray_result.position)
```


As test to see if ray is blocked
```gdscript
var params = PhysicsRayQueryParameters3D.create(Vector3.ZERO, Vector3(0, 0, 100))
var hit := space_state.test_ray(params)
```
